newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-BENETTON STRONG ENOUGH TO WIN TITLE, SAYS BERGER.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-BENETTON STRONG ENOUGH TO WIN TITLE, SAYS BERGER.

text.p: Gerhard Berger, at 37 the oldest and most experienced driver in Formula One, said on Thursday that Benetton would consider the 1997 season a failure if they did not win the championship.

Speaking at his team's launch amid the glitz and glamour of the Planet Hollywood restaurant in London, Berger said he had been impressed with the B197 car, powered by Renault's latest and lightest V10 engine.

"We have done some good testing and we were at the top of the times, which was good, but more important we have shown we are reliable," he explained. "Compared to last year we are much further ahead now and better prepared.
"It was very difficult for me last year because we had so many changes in the team but now we are more settled and the team feel very strong to me.
"I know this is only the launch and the truth will come later but I feel good. We are here this year to win the championship again and if we do not we will not have succeeded."
Berger, a veteran of 196 grands prix, said he felt better motivated than ever before as he prepared for his first race with Benetton after rejoining them from Ferrari.

Benetton team boss Flavio Briatore predicted that Benetton would be strong challengers and would make up for a disappointing 1996 season. They failed to win a race but finished third in the title race.
He said the team's budget was about $50 million and added that he was confident the ex-Ferrari pair of Berger and Jean Alesi would repay the team's faith in them this year.
"We feel prepared and able to pose a serious challenge this year to our main competitors," said Briatore who tipped Ferrari to win the world title.
"Williams, as usual, will be stable and competitive," said Briatore. "But McLaren will be strong too -- and so will we. It will be a very open and exciting championship."
